experimental_method: Analytic: water presaturated with nitrogen is brought to temperature and pressure in a high-pressure solubility pipet in a copper-block thermostat, stirred, and a sample withdrawn through a needle valve into a weighed trap; evolved gas dried through CaCl2 and measured in a gas buret over mercury.
uncertainties_stated: None stated in the text for the solubility values.
quality_remarks: Authors say Henry constants calculated from the data show wide variations and no significant trend. Pressures measured with a dead-weight piston gage. Nitrogen purified over hot copper wire and soda lime. 1931 scan, no temperature scale given, standard conditions for the gas volume not defined.
not_extracted_tables: Table II (Henry's law constant, derived by authors from Table I with fugacities): derived

row_counts.Table I: printed 4 data rows x 7 temperature columns = 28 values (plus a 1/T row); written 28 rows in long form

extraction_notes: Text layer matched the zoomed page image in every cell (checked at about 2.5x enlargement). The scan is somewhat noisy but legible. The PDF is a 4-page article with no foreign pages. Sanity: at each pressure the coefficient has a minimum near 80-100 C; increases with pressure at each temperature.
